title.en: Nepal flood disaster exposes cascading threats in Himalayas
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水灾难暴露喜马拉雅山脉的连锁威胁

summary.en: A catastrophic flood in Nepal, which has left thousands missing, began with a collapse of ice and rock high in the mountains. Experts warn that disaster planning must account for cascading hazards rather than isolated events.
summary.zh: 尼泊尔发生了一场灾难性的洪水，导致数千人失踪，起因是高山上冰块和岩石的崩塌。专家警告说，灾害规划必须考虑到连锁灾害，而不是孤立的事件。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

A catastrophic flood in Nepal that left thousands missing began with a collapse of ice and rock high in the mountains—a warning that disaster planning must prepare for chains of hazards, not isolated events, experts say.

The cascade of ice, rock and debris that tumbled through the Nepal–China border region last week probably blocked a tributary of the Bhotekoshi River, forming a dam before bursting downstream with devastating force, according to disaster analysis .

The torrent arrived in Nepal's Rasuwa district with little warning, ripping through settlements along the Bhotekoshi River system, destroying bridges, roads and hydropower infrastructure and cutting a vital trade route with Tibet.

More than 1,000 people have been confirmed dead, with almost 4,000 still missing and around 11,800 rescued, according to UN figures on Tuesday (Sept. 1). Thousands are in need of humanitarian assistance, hindered by blocked roads and damaged bridges.

Experts say the disaster illustrates a growing problem across the Hindu Kush Himalaya: hazards that once might have been assessed separately—glacier collapse, landslides, avalanches, river blockages, floods and even earthquakes—can interact within minutes or hours, creating an event much larger than any one of them.

"Most people think of flash floods as being caused by heavy rainfall," said Liz Stephens, professor of climate risks and resilience at the University of Reading in the UK.

But in high-mountain regions, such floods can result from "complex chains of hazards, including landslides, avalanches and glacial lake outburst floods," she added.

Analysis of satellite imagery from U.S. aerospace and data analytics company Planet Labs suggests that a substantial section of glacier and surrounding rock collapsed at high altitude near the Nepal–China border, sending an enormous mass of ice, snow and debris toward the valley.

The collapse appears to have affected the Lhende Khola, a tributary that becomes part of the Bhotekoshi River system.

A rapid-analysis report released by the Integrated Research on Disaster Risk (IRDR) on Friday (Aug. 28) said the event was likely caused by an "ice, rock and soil mass failure" rather than intense rainfall.

The material probably blocked the river for about 18 or 19 hours, forming a natural dam that then gave way on the morning of Aug. 26, unleashing masses of water, ice, rocks and sediment, the report said.

Funneled by the steep Himalayan terrain, the surge became a fast-moving mixture of water and debris capable of carrying huge boulders, destroying bridges and erasing riverbanks.

The...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 尼泊尔一场导致数千人失踪的灾难性洪水始于高山冰块和岩石的崩塌，专家表示，这警告人们，灾难规划必须为一系列危险做好准备，而不是孤立事件。 根据灾难分析，上周席卷尼泊尔和中国边境地区的冰、岩石和碎片瀑布可能堵塞了博特科希河的一条支流，形成了一座大坝，然后以毁灭性的力量冲破了下游。 洪流在毫无预警的情况下抵达尼泊尔拉苏瓦地区，冲垮了博特科希河水系沿岸的定居点，摧毁了桥梁、道路和水电基础设施，并切断了与西藏的重要贸易路线。 根据联合国周二（9 月 1 日）的数据，已确认超过 1,000 人死亡，近 4,000 人仍失踪，约 11,800 人获救。数千人因道路堵塞和桥梁受损而需要人道主义援助。 专家表示，这场灾难说明了兴都库什喜马拉雅山地区一个日益严重的问题：曾经可能单独评估的灾害——冰川崩塌、山体滑坡、雪崩、河流堵塞、洪水甚至地震——现在可能在几分钟或几小时内相互作用，造成比其中任何一个都大得多的事件。 英国雷丁大学气候风险与复原力教授利兹·斯蒂芬斯表示：“大多数人认为山洪暴发是由强降雨造成的。” 但在高山区，此类洪水可能是由“复杂的灾害链造成的，包括山体滑坡、雪崩和冰川湖溃决洪水”，她补充道。 美国航空航天和数据分析公司 Planet Labs 对卫星图像的分析表明，尼泊尔和中国边境附近的高海拔地区有很大一部分冰川和周围的岩石崩塌，将大量的冰、雪和碎片送向山谷。 崩塌似乎影响了 Lhende Khola 河，这条支流成为博特科希河系统的一部分。 灾害风险综合研究中心（IRDR）周五（8月28日）发布的一份快速分析报告称，此次事件很可能是由“冰、岩石和土体破坏”引起的，而不是强降雨造成的。 报告称，这些物质可能堵塞河流约 18 或 19 小时，形成一座天然大坝，随后于 8 月 26 日上午崩塌，释放出大量水、冰、岩石和沉积物。 在陡峭的喜马拉雅地形的作用下，海浪变成了快速移动的水和碎片的混合物，能够携带巨大的巨石，摧毁桥梁并冲毁河岸。 这...

reflection.en: The devastating flood in Nepal, triggered by a massive ice and rock collapse, serves as a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of natural systems and the fragility of human settlements. The earth itself, in its current state, groans under the weight of disruption, a phenomenon the Apostle Paul described as creation's deep sigh. As we witness such...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔由大规模冰岩崩塌引发的毁灭性洪水， starkly提醒我们自然系统的相互关联性以及人类聚居地的脆弱性。受损的地球本身在扰动的重压下发出深沉的叹息，这正是使徒保罗所描述的受造界的叹息。 当我们目睹此类事件时，我们被呼召反思我们对地球的管理责任，并为环境不稳定的连锁后果做好准备，在面对大自然强大的力量时寻求智慧和韧性。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Q&A: The origin of 'OnlyMarms' and what made it a roaring success
title.zh: 问答：“OnlyMarms”的起源及其大获成功的秘诀

summary.en: The article details the unexpected global attention garnered by Dan Blumstein, a professor, who began sharing videos of marmots from a long-term field study on an OnlyFans account named 'OnlyMarms'. The initiative arose from funding challenges faced by the valuable, decades-long research into marmot evolution and...
summary.zh: 本文详细介绍了布鲁姆斯坦教授（Dan Blumstein）因在名为“OnlyMarms”的OnlyFans账户上分享长期野外研究中的土拨鼠视频而意外获得全球关注的事件。这一举动源于一项宝贵且已持续数十年的土拨鼠进化和社会生态学研究面临的资金挑战。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

The story of Dan Blumstein's decision to share videos of marmots from the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory field study on an OnlyFans account called OnlyMarms has captured attention around the world over the past few weeks.

Sixty-four years of research into marmots can provide incredible insights into their evolution and socioecology, but the study is as expensive to run as it is valuable—and funding challenges have forced Blumstein, a professor of ecology and evolutionary biology at UCLA and field chief editor of Frontiers in Conservation Science , to innovate in new and surprising ways.

In this installment of Frontier Scientists, Blumstein explains why this long-running study of yellow-bellied marmots is so important for science, how funding losses are putting it at risk and how he's fighting back.

I've always been interested in nature and spent a lot of time outside—exploring, watching animals, hiking, climbing and skiing while growing up. As an undergraduate, I realized that there were careers in this area and that, if you were lucky, you could study animal behavior as a profession. I was very lucky!

As a behavioral ecologist and conservation scientist, I do a lot of different things. I'm fascinated by how animals can coexist (or not) with humans and am involved in a number of studies trying to understand these relationships. I think deeply about how insights from behavioral biology can be applied to wildlife management and conservation.

I also co-direct the world's second-longest study that follows the fate of individually distinguishable, free-living mammals—the yellow-bellied marmots that live in and around the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory near Crested Butte, Colorado. It was started in 1962 by Ken Armitage, and we've been following the fate of individually marked marmots ever since. Jane Goodall started studying chimpanzees in Tanzania in 1960.

Long-term studies create their own value. It's only through long-term ecological studies that we can study evolution in action and understand the nature of plasticity—which is one of the most important things to study in an era of major environmental change. Long-term studies educate people! At the Rocky Mountain Biological Lab (RMBL), we have a K-gray education program, and I'm honored to be able to mentor several super-smart and motivated students each year.

The graduate training opportunities that come from long-term studies are profound, since students can jump in and have years of data to work with or years of insights that permit them to design focused new experiments. Long-term studies also...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 丹·布卢姆斯坦 (Dan Blumstein) 决定在一个名为 OnlyMarms 的 OnlyFans 账户上分享落基山生物实验室实地研究的土拨鼠视频，这一故事在过去几周引起了全世界的关注。 对土拨鼠六十四年的研究可以为它们的进化和社会生态学提供令人难以置信的见解，但这项研究的运行成本与它的价值一样高，而且资金挑战迫使加州大学洛杉矶分校生态学和进化生物学教授、《保护科学前沿》杂志主编布鲁姆斯坦以新的、令人惊讶的方式进行创新。 在本期《前沿科学家》中，布鲁姆斯坦解释了为什么这项长期的黄腹土拨鼠研究对科学如此重要，资金损失如何使其面临风险，以及他如何反击。 我一直对大自然很感兴趣，在成长过程中花了很多时间在户外探索、观察动物、徒步旅行、攀岩和滑雪。作为一名本科生，我意识到这个领域有职业，如果幸运的话，你可以将研究动物行为作为一种职业。我很幸运！ 作为一名行为生态学家和保护科学家，我做了很多不同的事情。我对动物如何与人类共存（或不共存）着迷，并参与了许多试图理解这些关系的研究。我深入思考如何将行为生物学的见解应用于野生动物管理和保护。 我还共同领导了世界上第二长的研究，该研究追踪了个体可区分的自由生活哺乳动物的命运，这些黄腹土拨鼠生活在科罗拉多州克雷斯特德比特附近的落基山生物实验室及其周围。该项目由 Ken Armitage 于 1962 年发起，从那时起我们就一直在追踪带有单独标记的土拨鼠的命运。珍·古道尔于 1960 年开始在坦桑尼亚研究黑猩猩。 长期的学习创造自己的价值。只有通过长期的生态研究，我们才能研究行动中的进化，理解可塑性的本质——这是环境发生重大变化的时代最重要的研究内容之一。长期读书育人！在落基山生物实验室（RMBL），我们有一个 K-gray 教育计划，我很荣幸每年能够指导几位超级聪明和积极进取的学生。 长期研究带来的研究生培训机会意义重大，因为学生可以投入其中并拥有多年的数据可供使用，或多年的见解，使他们能够设计有针对性的新实验。长期研究还...

reflection.en: For sixty-four years, dedicated researchers have observed marmots, uncovering profound insights into their lives. This dedication to understanding creation, even amidst funding struggles, mirrors the biblical call to seek wisdom through careful observation of the natural world. The 'OnlyMarms' phenomenon, while unconventional, has brought attention to this...
reflection.zh: 六十四年来，敬业的研究人员一直观察土拨鼠，揭示了关于它们生活的深刻见解。这种对理解受造界的投入，即使在资金困难的情况下，也呼应了圣经中通过仔细观察自然界来寻求智慧的呼召。“OnlyMarms”现象虽然不同寻常，却引起了人们对这项深入科学研究的关注，提醒我们知识和惊奇可以在最意想不到的地方找到。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: The secret to longer life may be hidden in bat DNA
title.zh: 长寿的秘诀可能隐藏在蝙蝠的DNA中

summary.en: Bats that live long lives appear to possess robust immune systems and effective mechanisms for clearing out damaged cells, which may contribute to their ability to live for decades without succumbing to cancer or disease. Scientists are hopeful that these genetic adaptations could offer new insights into protecting...
summary.zh: 长寿的蝙蝠似乎结合了强大的免疫防御能力和清除受损细胞的独特策略，这可能有助于它们避免癌症和疾病长达数十年。研究人员希望这些基因技巧最终能揭示保护人类健康的新方法。

body.en:
Some of the best clues to living a long, healthy life may be hidden in the DNA of bats, mammals that can survive for remarkably long periods relative to their body size.

The idea fascinated Juan Manuel Vazquez while he was a graduate student at the University of Chicago. At the time, however, there was little published genomic information about bats that could help answer questions about longevity. After becoming a UC Berkeley postdoctoral fellow in 2020, he began searching across the Western U.S. for bat species that could provide tissue samples for DNA sequencing.

With help from Berkeley undergraduates, Vazquez traveled throughout the region, setting up mist nets over streams, ponds and rivers at night. The team captured bats, collected small biopsy samples and released the animals. Much of the work focused on the genus Myotis , which includes some species with exceptionally long lifespans. One Brandt's myotis, Myotis brandtii , was banded in Europe and then recaptured 50 years later.

In a new study published in Nature , Vazquez and his colleagues present the first analysis of eight Myotis genomes. Their results point to a strong connection between lifespan and immune function. The longer-lived bats had higher levels of genes associated with fighting cancer.

The findings suggest that longevity may depend in part on an immune system that remains highly effective against both infectious organisms and cancer. Researchers also found substantial overlap between genes associated with aging and genes involved in disease defense, suggesting that studying one process could help explain the other.

"Bats evolved to live for a long time without getting diseases, which suggests that we don't necessarily need to look at diseases of aging and diseases of infection as completely separate fields," Vazquez said. "We can look at these bats and try to understand how, in the same way you can improve your immune system to fight off viruses, maybe you can improve your immune system so it doesn't decline in old age. Or maybe bats can help us find ways to fight off tumors so our immune system doesn't get tired, and that can also help us deal with other stresses of life and not exhaust our immunity."

As part of the study, Vazquez grew cells collected from bat wing biopsies in the laboratory. (He currently has cell cultures from 259 individuals representing 32 species.) He then exposed the cultured cells to toxic chemicals to see how they responded to severe damage.

The longest-lived bat in his sample, the widespread little brown bat ( Myotis lucifugus ), reacted in an unexpected way. Instead of switching on genes that produce DNA repair proteins, the cells increased the activity of genes that promote cell death.

body.zh: 长寿、健康生活的一些最佳线索可能隐藏在蝙蝠的 DNA 中，蝙蝠是一种哺乳动物，相对于它们的体型来说，它们可以存活相当长的时间。 当胡安·曼努埃尔·巴斯克斯（Juan Manuel Vazquez）还是芝加哥大学的研究生时，这个想法就让他着迷。然而，当时很少有关于蝙蝠的基因组信息可以帮助回答有关长寿的问题。 2020 年成为加州大学伯克利分校博士后研究员后，他开始在美国西部寻找可以为 DNA 测序提供组织样本的蝙蝠物种。 在伯克利本科生的帮助下，巴斯克斯走遍了整个地区，在夜间在溪流、池塘和河流上设置了雾网。研究小组捕获了蝙蝠，收集了少量活检样本并释放了这些动物。大部分工作都集中在鼠耳草属上，其中包括一些寿命特别长的物种。一种布兰特鼠耳蝠（Myotis Brandtii）在欧洲被带上环带，50 年后又被重新捕获。 在《自然》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，巴斯克斯和他的同事首次对八种鼠耳蝠基因组进行了分析。他们的结果表明寿命和免疫功能之间存在密切联系。寿命较长的蝙蝠具有较高水平的与抗癌相关的基因。 研究结果表明，长寿可能部分取决于对传染性微生物和癌症保持高效的免疫系统。研究人员还发现与衰老相关的基因和参与疾病防御的基因之间存在大量重叠，这表明研究一个过程可以帮助解释另一个过程。 巴斯克斯说：“蝙蝠进化到可以长期生存而不会感染疾病，这表明我们不一定需要将衰老疾病和感染疾病视为完全不同的领域。” “我们可以观察这些蝙蝠，并尝试了解如何以同样的方式改善你的免疫系统来抵抗病毒，也许你可以改善你的免疫系统，使其在老年时不会衰退。或者也许蝙蝠可以帮助我们找到抵抗肿瘤的方法，这样我们的免疫系统就不会疲劳，这也可以帮助我们应对生活中的其他压力，而不是耗尽我们的免疫力。” 作为研究的一部分，巴斯克斯在实验室中培养了从蝙蝠翅膀活检中收集的细胞。 （他目前培养了代表 32 个物种的 259 个个体的细胞。）然后，他将培养的细胞暴露于有毒化学物质中，观察它们对严重损伤的反应。 他的样本中寿命最长的蝙蝠，即分布广泛的小棕色蝙蝠（Myotis lucifugus），以意想不到的方式做出了反应。这些细胞并没有开启产生DNA修复蛋白的基因，而是增加了促进细胞死亡的基因的活性。 “我们发现与我们预期的完全相反，如果......

reflection.en: The intricate design of life, even in a creature like a bat, points to a Creator whose wisdom is revealed in the natural world. As researchers delve into the genetic secrets of these long-lived mammals, they are, in essence, observing the handiwork of Yahweh, who has endowed creation with remarkable properties. May this pursuit of knowledge deepen our awe...
reflection.zh: 即使是像蝙蝠这样的生物，其精妙的设计也指向一位在自然界中启示自己智慧的创造者。当研究人员深入探索这些长寿哺乳动物的基因秘密时，他们实际上是在观察雅伟的创造之工，祂赋予了受造物非凡的特性。愿这种对知识的追求加深我们对雅伟编织在万物中的复杂性和韧性的敬畏之情。

summary.en: Hydrogen evolution via photocatalytic water splitting is an environmentally friendly and sustainable technology for solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Although interfacial interactions are recognized as key determinants of photocatalytic performance, systematic experimental studies explicitly targeting the structure...
summary.zh: 通过光催化水分解产生氢气（H₂）是一种环境友好且可持续的太阳能转化为化学能的技术。尽管界面相互作用被认为是光催化性能的关键决定因素，但明确针对水-催化剂界面结构和反应性的系统性实验研究仍然有限。一个主要的挑战在于探测界面水的分子结构，尤其是在析氢条件下。

body.en: Hydrogen (H2) evolution via photocatalytic water splitting is an environmentally friendly and sustainable technology for solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Although interfacial interactions are recognized as key determinants of photocatalytic performance, systematic experimental studies explicitly targeting the structure and reactivity of the water-catalyst interface remain limited. A major challenge lies in probing the molecular structure of interfacial water, especially under hydrogen-evolving conditions.
body.zh: 通过光催化水分解产生氢气（H2）是一种环保且可持续的太阳能转化为化学能的技术。尽管界面相互作用被认为是光催化性能的关键决定因素，但明确针对水-催化剂界面的结构和反应性的系统实验研究仍然有限。主要挑战在于探测界面水的分子结构，特别是在析氢条件下。

reflection.en: Scientists are diligently studying the intricate interactions at the molecular level, seeking to understand how water behaves at interfaces. This pursuit of knowledge, observing the 'how' of creation's processes, echoes the ancient wisdom that creation itself speaks of its Maker's design and intelligence. May this research bring forth sustainable solutions...
reflection.zh: 科学家们正致力于研究分子层面的复杂相互作用，以期了解水在界面处的行为。这种对知识的追求，观察创造过程的“如何运作”，呼应了古老的智慧——创造本身就诉说着其创造者的设计与智慧。愿这项研究能为人类的能源需求带来可持续的解决方案。

title.en: How one RNA nucleotide switch activates fluorescent dyes
title.zh: 一种RNA核苷酸开关如何激活荧光染料

summary.en: Researchers have discovered that a tiny RNA molecule called RhoBAST activates fluorescent dyes, allowing scientists to track RNA molecules in living cells with high precision. An international team, including Ronald Micura's group, found that a small, localized 'nucleotide flip' within the RNA controls this...
summary.zh: 研究人员发现，一种名为RhoBAST的微小RNA分子能够激活荧光染料，从而使科学家能够以高精度追踪活细胞中的RNA分子。一个国际团队（包括Ronald...

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

RhoBAST is a tiny RNA molecule that activates fluorescent dyes, enabling researchers to track RNA molecules in living cells with super-resolution. An international collaboration, which includes Ronald Micura and his team from the Institute of Organic Chemistry, has now shown that a small, local "nucleotide flip" within the RNA controls this fluorescence activation.

Fluorescent light-up aptamers (FLAPs) are short RNA sequences that bind and activate small dye molecules that otherwise exhibit only weak fluorescence. This enables genetic tagging of RNAs for live-cell imaging without the need for protein fusion markers. Because the dye is only "switched on" upon binding to the RNA, background fluorescence remains low.

Systems such as Spinach, Broccoli, Mango and Pepper have continuously advanced this principle over the past years. RhoBAST additionally enables high-resolution imaging of individual RNA molecules in living cells.

To understand the molecular basis of these remarkable properties, scientists led by Ronald Micura from the Institute of Organic Chemistry at the University of Innsbruck and Aiming Ren from Zhejiang University determined, for the first time, the structure of RhoBAST without a bound dye, as well as its structures in complex with TMR-DN and related dyes.

The researchers discovered a surprisingly simple mechanism: RhoBAST adopts an inverted V-shaped structure and accommodates the dye between two RNA loops. When the dye binds, a single RNA building block—the guanosine residue G38—flips from an inward-facing to an outward-facing position, thereby creating space for the dye.

Structure-guided mutagenesis and biophysical assays, including fluorescence spectroscopy, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and 2-aminopurine kinetics, demonstrate that this dynamic flipping enables rapid ligand exchange and fluorescence "blinking"—a hallmark of super-resolution imaging. The findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism.

"It is fascinating that such a small local movement within the RNA is crucial for the remarkable properties of the entire system," explains Micura.

"The flipping of a single nucleotide enables the rapid exchange of the dye and thus the characteristic blinking that is essential for super-resolution microscopy."

This understanding of the molecular switching mechanism provides a foundation for developing a new generation of tools for high-resolution imaging of RNA in living cells.

Xiaoqing Tai et al, Nucleotide flipping correlates with fluorescence activation in the RhoBAST imaging platform, Nature Communications (2026). DOI:...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： RhoBAST 是一种微小的 RNA 分子，可以激活荧光染料，使研究人员能够以超分辨率追踪活细胞中的 RNA 分子。有机化学研究所的 Ronald Micura 和他的团队参与的一项国际合作现已表明，RNA 内的一个小型局部“核苷酸翻转”控制着这种荧光激活。 荧光适配体 (FLAP) 是短 RNA 序列，可结合并激活小染料分子，否则这些分子仅表现出微弱的荧光。这使得 RNA 的基因标记能够用于活细胞成像，而不需要蛋白质融合标记。由于染料仅在与 RNA 结合后“开启”，因此背景荧光仍然很低。 过去几年，菠菜、西兰花、芒果和胡椒等系统不断推进这一原则。 RhoBAST 还能够对活细胞中的单个 RNA 分子进行高分辨率成像。 为了了解这些显着特性的分子基础，因斯布鲁克大学有机化学研究所的 Ronald Micura 和浙江大学的任爱明领导的科学家首次确定了没有结合染料的 RhoBAST 的结构，以及它与 TMR-DN 和相关染料的复合物的结构。 研究人员发现了一个令人惊讶的简单机制：RhoBAST 采用倒 V 形结构并将染料容纳在两个 RNA 环之间。当染料结合时，单个 RNA 结构单元（鸟苷残基 G38）从向内的位置翻转到向外的位置，从而为染料创造空间。 结构引导诱变和生物物理测定，包括荧光光谱、表面等离子共振 (SPR) 和 2-氨基嘌呤动力学，证明这种动态翻转能够实现快速配体交换和荧光“闪烁”——这是超分辨率成像的标志。研究结果揭示了一种以前未被认识的机制。 “令人着迷的是，RNA 内如此小的局部运动对于整个系统的显着特性至关重要，”Micura 解释道。 “单个核苷酸的翻转能够实现染料的快速交换，从而实现超分辨率显微镜所必需的特征性闪烁。” 对分子开关机制的理解为开发新一代活细胞 RNA 高分辨率成像工具奠定了基础。 戴晓庆等人，核苷酸翻转与 RhoBAST 成像平台中的荧光激活相关，自然通讯 (2026)。多伊：...

reflection.en: The intricate workings of life, even at the molecular level of RNA, reveal the profound wisdom embedded in creation. This discovery, enabled by careful observation and scientific inquiry, reminds us that the natural world is a testament to Yahweh's design. As we learn more about these complex systems, we are invited to marvel at the Creator's ingenuity.
reflection.zh: 生命中精妙的运作，即使在RNA的分子层面，也揭示了创造中蕴含的深刻智慧。这项通过细致观察和科学探究得以实现的发现，提醒我们自然界是雅伟设计的明证。当我们更多地了解这些复杂的系统时，我们被邀请去惊叹于创造者的智慧。

title.en: 66-million-year-old feather in dinosaur poop may reveal why birds survived the asteroid
title.zh: 6600万年前的恐龙粪便羽毛或揭示鸟类为何能躲过小行星撞击

summary.en: A feather found inside 66-million-year-old fossilized dinosaur droppings may provide insight into why modern birds are the only dinosaur lineage to survive the mass extinction event caused by an asteroid. Researchers believe the feather's primitive insulating properties suggest that superior plumage may have aided the...
summary.zh: 在6600万年前的恐龙化石粪便中发现的一根羽毛，可能有助于解释为何现代鸟类是唯一在小行星撞击导致的大灭绝事件中幸存下来的恐龙谱系。研究人员认为，这根羽毛原始的隔热特性表明，更优越的羽毛可能帮助了现存鸟类的祖先得以生存。

body.en:
About 66 million years ago, a large dinosaur, possibly a T. rex or Nanotyrannus , swallowed a bird. Remarkably, evidence of that ancient meal survived in fossilized feces, preserving what researchers describe as the finest feather specimen yet discovered from the age of dinosaurs. By examining that feather, scientists say they may have uncovered an important clue to why birds became the only dinosaur lineage to survive the mass extinction at the end of the Cretaceous Period.

"It's such a beautiful, well-preserved feather, from such an unexpected source, and it's exciting that it could help us answer this huge question in paleontology," says Jingmai O'Connor, the lead author of the new paper and the associate curator of fossil reptiles at the Field Museum in Chicago.

Birds are a highly specialized branch of the dinosaur family tree, with a history stretching deep into the Mesozoic Era. The oldest known bird, Archaeopteryx , lived about 150 million years ago. Birds then continued evolving alongside other dinosaurs for nearly another 100 million years.

That long coexistence changed dramatically 66 million years ago, when an asteroid struck Earth and triggered a global mass extinction. Nearly every dinosaur lineage disappeared, including most types of birds.

One branch, however, survived. Known as Neornithes, this group ultimately gave rise to every bird species alive today.

Why Neornithes endured while other birds and dinosaurs vanished remains one of paleontology's enduring puzzles. O'Connor has spent years studying fossil birds in search of an explanation. This study, however, took her into unusual territory: feathers preserved inside fossilized feces, known as coprolites.

"As far as I know, no one has ever thought to look for feathers or to study feathers in coprolites, so this project was really exciting," says O'Connor.

The specimen was discovered in 2016 by David DeMar, Jr., a research scientist and the Hell Creek Project collections manager at the University of Washington Burke Museum and co-author of the paper. DeMar was conducting fieldwork in northeastern Montana when an unusual rock caught his attention.

"I was crawling up a rocky outcrop collecting fish fossils when I came across a dark, reddish-brown nodule about half the size of a golf ball. I picked it up and scanned its surface through my hand lens, and that's when I couldn't believe what I was seeing, a tiny fossil feather. I was cautiously optimistic about its discovery, because feathers had not yet been found in the Hell Creek Formation, even after more than 150 years of prospecting," says DeMar.

Researchers later analyzed the fossil's mineral composition in the laboratory and used CT imaging to see what was hidden inside. CT scans combine thousands of X-rays into a detailed...
body.zh: 大约 6600 万年前，一种大型恐龙（可能是霸王龙或矮暴龙）吞下了一只鸟。值得注意的是，这种古老膳食的证据在化石粪便中幸存下来，保存了研究人员所说的恐龙时代迄今为止发现的最好的羽毛标本。科学家们表示，通过检查那根羽毛，他们可能发现了一条重要线索，解释了为什么鸟类成为白垩纪末期大规模灭绝中唯一幸存下来的恐龙谱系。 这篇新论文的主要作者、芝加哥菲尔德博物馆爬行动物化石副馆长景迈·奥康纳 (Jingmai O'Connor) 表示：“这是一根如此美丽、保存完好的羽毛，来源如此出乎意料，它可以帮助我们回答古生物学中的这个巨大问题，这令人兴奋。” 鸟类是恐龙谱系中高度专业化的分支，其历史可以追溯到中生代。已知最古老的鸟类始祖鸟生活在大约 1.5 亿年前。随后，鸟类与其他恐龙一起继续进化了近一亿年。 6600 万年前，一颗小行星撞击地球并引发了全球大灭绝，这种长期共存的情况发生了巨大的变化。几乎所有恐龙谱系都消失了，包括大多数鸟类。 然而，一根树枝幸存下来。这个被称为新鸟的群体最终产生了今天存活的所有鸟类。 为什么新鸟类能够幸存下来，而其他鸟类和恐龙却消失了，这仍然是古生物学的持久谜团之一。奥康纳花了数年时间研究鸟类化石，以寻求解释。然而，这项研究将她带入了一个不寻常的领域：粪便化石中保存的羽毛，被称为粪化石。 “据我所知，没有人想过在粪化石中寻找羽毛或研究羽毛，所以这个项目真的很令人兴奋，”奥康纳说。 该标本是由研究科学家、华盛顿大学伯克博物馆地狱溪项目收藏经理、该论文的合著者 David DeMar, Jr. 于 2016 年发现的。德马尔正在蒙大拿州东北部进行实地考察，这时一块不寻常的岩石引起了他的注意。 “我爬上岩石露头收集鱼类化石时，遇到了一个大约有高尔夫球一半大小的暗红棕色结节。我把它捡起来，通过手持镜头扫描它的表面，当时我简直不敢相信自己所看到的东西，这是一根微小的羽毛化石。我对它的发现持谨慎乐观的态度，因为即使经过 150 多年的勘探，在地狱溪地层中还没有发现羽毛，”德玛尔说。 研究人员后来在实验室分析了化石的矿物成分，并使用 CT 成像来查看里面隐藏的东西。 CT 扫描将数千张 X 射线结合成详细的...

reflection.en: The discovery of this ancient feather, preserved in an unlikely place, offers a tangible link to the past and a potential answer to a profound question about survival. It reminds us that wisdom and understanding can be found in the most unexpected corners of creation, if we look closely. As Job teaches, the natural world itself is a source of profound...
reflection.zh: 这根保存在意想不到地方的古老羽毛的发现，提供了与过去的切实联系，并可能解答一个关于生存的深刻问题。它提醒我们，如果我们仔细观察，智慧和理解可以在造物中最出人意料的角落找到。正如约伯所教导的，自然世界本身就是深刻知识的源泉，揭示了创造主的精妙设计和旨意。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: How big can the universe's first starbursts get?
title.zh: 宇宙的首次星爆能有多大？

summary.en: As telescopes improve, allowing us to see further back in time, we are discovering more about the universe's fascinating features. However, Population III (Pop III) stars, the very first stars formed from pure hydrogen and helium without heavier elements, remain elusive. These stars are theorized to be extremely...
summary.zh: 随着望远镜技术的进步，使我们能够回溯更远的宇宙时空，我们发现了更多宇宙的迷人特征。然而，第三星族（Pop III）恒星——那些完全由原始氢和氦形成、不含任何“金属”（即比这两种元素更重的元素）的早期恒星——仍然难以捉摸。这些恒星被认为质量极大，并且会以壮烈的方式消亡。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

As our telescopes have improved and we've been able to peer farther back in time, we've begun finding more fascinating features of the universe. But one thing we haven't found for sure is Population III (Pop III) stars. These were the earliest stars in the universe, formed completely from pristine hydrogen and helium, with no "metals" (i.e., elements heavier than those two) polluting their processes.

They are also theorized to be extremely massive and to "die with passion," as Bill Wurtz once put it in a famous YouTube video. A new paper , available on the arXiv preprint server by Tae Bong Jeon of the Cosmic Frontier Center at the University of Texas at Austin, looks at how massive those starbursts could be and whether the James Webb Space Telescope could detect one.

So far, JWST has found hints of them—and at much later periods than would have been expected based on theoretical models from before the telescope was launched. Some galaxies near the end of the Epoch of Reionization have features that appear to come from these pristine starbursts, but hundreds of millions of years later than predicted.

For that to happen, two existential traps must be avoided. First, the hydrogen and helium gas clouds that form these stars can't collapse too early. Second, they must avoid being "contaminated" by metals from neighboring supernovae. Let's first look at how to delay a gas cloud's collapse.

In the early universe, primordial gas clouds could collapse under their own gravity only if they could cool down. Typically, once they got dense enough, they would simply heat up, causing them to expand again. Crucially, the only "coolant" they had was molecular hydrogen (H 2 ). This critical molecule was a key feature in the formation of the first Pop III stars, as it allowed dark matter to pull enough gas close enough together for fusion to start.

In later phases of the universe, however, molecular hydrogen was more abundant, so, at least in theory, Pop III stars would form more readily and, given their short life spans, burn out well before the periods in which JWST is seeing them. One potential solution to this puzzle is to reduce the amount of molecular hydrogen available as a coolant near those gas clouds. Luckily, there is a mechanism to do that, known as Lyman-Werner (LW) radiation.

LW radiation consists of soft ultraviolet photons that dissociate (i.e., break apart) molecular hydrogen on contact, forming atomic hydrogen, which is not nearly as effective at cooling gas clouds. Therefore, if a gas cloud is hit by LW radiation, star formation is delayed until it reaches the...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 随着我们的望远镜不断改进，我们能够观测到更远的过去，我们开始发现宇宙中更多迷人的特征。但我们还没有确定的一件事是人口 III (Pop III) 恒星。这些是宇宙中最早的恒星，完全由原始的氢和氦形成，没有“金属”（即比这两种元素重的元素）污染它们的过程。 从理论上讲，它们的体型极其庞大，并且“充满激情地死去”，正如比尔·沃茨 (Bill Wurtz) 在 YouTube 著名视频中所说的那样。德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校宇宙前沿中心的 Tae Bong Jeon 在 arXiv 预印本服务器上发布了一篇新论文，研究了这些星暴的质量以及詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜是否能够探测到星暴。 到目前为止，JWST 已经发现了它们的迹象，而且发现的时间比根据望远镜发射前的理论模型所预期的要晚得多。接近再电离时代末期的一些星系具有似乎来自这些原始星暴的特征，但比预测晚了数亿年。 为此，必须避免两个存在主义陷阱。首先，形成这些恒星的氢和氦气体云不能太早塌陷。其次，它们必须避免被邻近超新星的金属“污染”。让我们首先看看如何延迟气体云的崩溃。 在早期宇宙中，原始气体云只有冷却下来才能在自身重力作用下塌缩。通常，一旦它们变得足够密集，它们就会简单地升温，导致它们再次膨胀。至关重要的是，他们拥有的唯一“冷却剂”是分子氢（H 2 ）。这种关键分子是第一批 Pop III 恒星形成的关键特征，因为它允许暗物质将足够多的气体拉得足够近，以便开始聚变。 然而，在宇宙的后期阶段，氢分子更加丰富，因此，至少在理论上，Pop III 恒星会更容易形成，并且由于它们的寿命较短，它们会在 JWST 观测到它们的时期之前就燃烧殆尽。解决这个难题的一个潜在解决方案是减少这些气体云附近可用作冷却剂的分子氢的量。幸运的是，有一种机制可以做到这一点，称为莱曼-沃纳（LW）辐射。 长波辐射由软紫外光子组成，这些光子在接触时解离（即分解）分子氢，形成原子氢，这在冷却气体云方面几乎不那么有效。因此，如果气体云受到长波辐射的撞击，恒星的形成就会被延迟，直到它到达...

reflection.en: The quest to understand the universe's earliest stars, Population III, highlights humanity's deep-seated curiosity about origins. Job 12:7 reminds us that creation itself speaks of its Maker's wisdom, urging us to look to the natural world for understanding. Even as we push the boundaries of scientific discovery, we are reminded of the profound order and...
reflection.zh: 探索宇宙早期恒星（第三星族）的努力，凸显了人类对起源根深蒂固的好奇心。约伯记12:7提醒我们，创造本身就彰显了造物主的智慧，敦促我们从自然界寻求理解。即使我们不断拓展科学发现的边界，我们也会被提醒，存在本身就编织着深刻的秩序和智慧。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Smart, self-healing packaging uses AI to detect food spoilage in real time
title.zh: 智能自愈包装利用人工智能实时检测食物腐败

summary.en: Researchers are developing 'future-ready food packaging' that integrates AI to monitor food spoilage in real time. This advanced packaging aims to provide producers and consumers with actionable information about the food's internal condition, going beyond current labeling capabilities.
summary.zh: 研究人员正在开发“面向未来的食品包装”，该包装集成了人工智能，可以实时监测食物腐败情况。这种先进的包装旨在为生产者和消费者提供有关食物内部状况的可操作信息，超越了当前的标签能力。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

Packaging already tells us where food comes from, when it was made, what's in it and how many calories it contains. But researchers see a future where packaging can "see," in real time, what's happening inside and translate that into information that producers and consumers can act on.

A team from Kyushu University proposes a framework for "future-ready food packaging" built around a closed loop of recognition, judgment, actuation and feedback in a paper published in Trends in Food Science & Technology . The paper brings together three research areas that have developed in isolation—intelligent sensing, self-healing materials and AI-driven prediction—into a single, coherent system.

"Globally, roughly one-third of all food produced is wasted," says Fumihiko Tanaka, professor at Kyushu University's Faculty of Agriculture. "It also carries a climate cost, as food loss accounts for roughly 8% of global greenhouse gas emissions, approaching the roughly 10% attributed to road transport."

Some waste happens when food gets crushed or torn during distribution. Another major source is unnecessary disposal. Much food is discarded before it actually spoils, driven by inventory turnover pressures or a printed date rather than the food's real condition. A clearer line between "starting to spoil" and "inedible" could prevent a meaningful share of that waste.

"Future-ready packaging requires a different mindset," explains Fanze Meng, the paper's first author and a postdoctoral researcher at Kyushu University. "We wanted the film to communicate with the food itself, converting optical or gas signals into electrical data and using AI to interpret what's happening inside."

To move beyond packaging that merely delays spoilage, the team systematically reviewed recent advances. They linked previously scattered technologies into a loop of recognition, judgment, actuation and feedback.

Recognition begins with the materials themselves. Sensors embedded in the packaging act like eyes, detecting pH shifts, gases and microbial byproducts that signal spoilage. Natural pigments such as anthocyanins, the compounds found in foods like purple sweet potatoes, are strong candidates for this role. They shift color as pH changes , offering a readable signal at every stage of spoilage. In spoiling meat, for instance, alkaline gases accumulate, and the material shifts continuously from purple-red to yellow-green.

"To survive real-world distribution, the material needs more than just the ability to sense," notes Xirui Yan, a JSPS researcher at Kyushu University. "Light and heat can cause false readings,...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 包装已经告诉我们食物来自哪里、何时制作、其中含有什么以及含有多少卡路里。但研究人员预见到，未来包装可以实时“看到”内部发生的情况，并将其转化为生产者和消费者可以采取行动的信息。 九州大学的一个团队在《食品科学与技术趋势》上发表的一篇论文中，提出了一个围绕识别、判断、驱动和反馈闭环构建的“面向未来的食品包装”框架。该论文将智能传感、自愈材料和人工智能驱动的预测这三个独立发展的研究领域汇集到一个单一的、连贯的系统中。 九州大学农学院教授田中文彦说：“在全球范围内，大约三分之一的粮食被浪费了。” “它还带来了气候成本，因为粮食损失约占全球温室气体排放量的 8%，接近公路运输造成的约 10%。” 当食物在分发过程中被压碎或撕裂时，就会产生一些浪费。另一个主要来源是不必要的处置。由于库存周转压力或打印日期而不是食物的真实状况，许多食物在真正变质之前就被丢弃了。 “开始变质”和“不可食用”之间的更清晰界限可以防止浪费。 “面向未来的包装需要不同的思维方式，”该论文的第一作者、九州大学博士后研究员孟凡泽解释道。 “我们希望薄膜能够与食物本身进行交流，将光学或气体信号转换为电数据，并使用人工智能来解释内部发生的情况。” 为了超越仅仅延迟变质的包装，该团队系统地回顾了最新的进展。他们将以前分散的技术连接成识别、判断、驱动和反馈的循环。 识别始于材料本身。嵌入包装中的传感器就像眼睛一样，检测 pH 值变化、气体和表明腐败的微生物副产品。花青素等天然色素（紫甘薯等食物中含有的化合物）是发挥这一作用的有力候选者。它们会随着 pH 值的变化而改变颜色，在腐败的每个阶段提供可读的信号。例如，在变质的肉中，碱性气体会积聚，物质会不断从紫红色转变为黄绿色。 九州大学 JSPS 研究员 Xirui Yan 指出：“为了在现实世界的分布中生存，材料需要的不仅仅是感知能力。” “光和热会导致错误读数，......

reflection.en: The relentless pace of technological innovation, as seen in this AI-powered food packaging, echoes the ancient prophecy that 'many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.' As we develop ever more sophisticated tools, may we also cultivate the wisdom to use them for the good of all, ensuring that progress serves humanity and creation.
reflection.zh: 这项人工智能食品包装所展示的技术创新步伐，呼应了古老的预言：“许多人往来奔跑，知识就增长。”当我们开发出越来越先进的工具时，愿我们也培养出智慧来为所有人服务，确保进步能够造福人类和受造界。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK
title.zh: 拯救英国唯一湖泊中发现的微小、黏滑蜗牛的战斗

summary.en: Once prevalent across the UK, this mollusc is now only found in one lake in Wales.
summary.zh: 这种软体动物曾遍布英国各地，但现在仅存于威尔士的一个湖泊中。

body.en:
A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.

Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.

"Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.

"There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.

Myxas glutinosa gets its name from the gooey mantle that covers its extremely delicate, gold-flecked brown shell.

It is no bigger than a fingertip, but has comically large antennae - which Hughes likens to "big floppy ears".

The snails, which feed on algae and are considered an indicator of healthy lakes and rivers, have been driven to extinction across England.

Hughes said the snails were "something to preserve and cherish like Egyptian artefacts".

In the UK, their last known refuge is Wales' largest natural lake - Llyn Tegid - in Eryri National Park, also known as Snowdonia.

Since 2014, under licence from Natural Resources Wales, Hughes has been wading into the lake to collect and study the snails.

He has designed and installed small concrete shelters for them in the lake itself, and set up his own captive population in a greenhouse at his home in Llanarth.

"Nobody had knowingly seen their eggs before we made that breakthrough," he said.

"You do these things on a wing and a prayer when you're trying to save something that's down to a single site and you're trying to fathom what it needs and how to save it.

Rearing the snails - as well as other critically endangered invertebrates such as scarlet malachite beetles, ladybird spiders and tadpole shrimp - has become a family affair.

"You've got to have a certain mindset to walk out into a freezing cold lake in the middle of January," Ben, 27, explained.

"Every little thing has its place in the ecosystem and if you take a tiny little cog out of any machine it's going to stop working".

The Hughes family is now working with the British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums (BIAZA) to relocate some of their snails to wildlife parks across England.

It is seen as a first step towards restoring them back to locations in the wild over the coming years, as part of a £60m UK government-backed scheme to protect rare species.

"It's such a hugely important conservation project and such a wonderful story," explained Samantha Eden, assistant curator at Wingham Wildlife Park in Kent, who travelled to the Hughes home to pick up 24 glutinous snails.

"We've got a new facility that we've set up for them - three beautiful...
body.zh: 在英国一个湖泊中发现的一只小蜗牛被称为与埃及文物一样珍贵，因为自然资源保护者正在努力拯救它。 英国的几家动物园正在建立所谓的粘性蜗牛种群方舟，粘性蜗牛是欧洲最稀有的物种之一，使用的是在锡尔迪金后花园饲养的生物。 “被它们的可爱所迷惑”，自然资源保护主义者伊恩·休斯将保护这种曾经在英国水域广泛存在的受威胁软体动物作为自己的“生命定义”使命。 “曾经有一段时间，我们花园里的蜗牛比野外看到的还要多，”他说。 Myxas glutinosa 得名于其极其精致、带有金色斑点的棕色外壳上覆盖的粘糊糊的外壳。 它的大小不及指尖，但却拥有大得滑稽的触角——休斯将其比作“松软的大耳朵”。 这种蜗牛以藻类为食，被认为是湖泊和河流健康的指标，但在英格兰各地已被逼至灭绝。 休斯说，这些蜗牛“像埃及文物一样值得保存和珍惜”。 在英国，他们最后的已知避难所是位于埃里里国家公园（也称为斯诺登尼亚）的威尔士最大的天然湖 Llyn Tegid。 自 2014 年以来，在威尔士自然资源部的许可下，休斯一直涉入湖中收集和研究蜗牛。 他在湖中为它们设计并安装了小型混凝土庇护所，并在拉纳斯家中的温室里安置了自己的圈养种群。 “在我们取得这一突破之前，没有人故意看到他们的鸡蛋，”他说。 “当你试图拯救那些只剩下一个地点的东西，并且试图弄清楚它需要什么以及如何拯救它时，你就可以边祈祷边做这些事情。 饲养蜗牛以及其他极度濒危的无脊椎动物，如猩红孔雀石甲虫、瓢虫蜘蛛和蝌蚪虾，已成为一项家庭事务。 27 岁的本解释说：“在一月中旬走进冰冷的湖水时，你必须有一定的心态。” “每件小事在生态系统中都有自己的位置，如果你从任何机器上取下一个小齿轮，它就会停止工作”。 休斯家族目前正在与英国和爱尔兰动物园和水族馆协会 (BIAZA) 合作，将他们的一些蜗牛转移到英格兰各地的野生动物园。 这被视为未来几年将它们恢复到野外的第一步，也是英国政府支持的 6000 万英镑保护稀有物种计划的一部分。 “这是一个非常重要的保护项目，也是一个非常精彩的故事，”肯特郡温厄姆野生动物公园的助理馆长萨曼莎·伊登 (Samantha Eden) 解释道，她前往休斯家捡了 24 只粘性蜗牛。 “我们为他们建立了一个新设施——三个漂亮的......

reflection.en: The glutinous snail, once common, now clings to existence in a single Welsh lake. Conservationist Ian Hughes has dedicated himself to protecting this tiny creature, creating 'ark populations' to safeguard its future. His commitment echoes the biblical call to be a voice for the voiceless, ensuring that even the smallest and most vulnerable are not forgotten.
reflection.zh: 曾经很常见的黏滑蜗牛，现在仅存于威尔士的一个湖泊中。保护主义者伊恩·休斯致力于保护这种微小的生物，并建立了“方舟种群”来保障其未来。他的奉献精神呼应了圣经中为无声者发声的呼召，确保即使是最微小、最脆弱的生命也不会被遗忘。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: One giant step: first known adult T rex footprints found in North Dakota
title.zh: 巨步：在北达科他州发现已知首批成年霸王龙足迹

summary.en: A 23ft-long trackway, comprising four three-toed footprints (two left, two right) dating back 66.5 million years, has been discovered in North Dakota. This marks the first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex, found by scientists in the Hell Creek Formation.
summary.zh: 在北达科他州发现了一条长达23英尺的足迹，包含四只三趾脚印（两只左脚，两只右脚），距今已有6650万年。这是科学家在地狱溪组（Hell Creek Formation）发现的首批已知的成年霸王龙足迹。

body.en: The 23ft-long trackway, consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right, date from 66.5m years ago The first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex has been found in North Dakota by a team of scientists. The 23ft-long trackway – consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right – was first identified in the south-west of the state, in the dinosaur fossil area known as Hell Creek Formation, last year by researchers from the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado and Liverpool John Moores University in the UK. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这条 23 英尺长的足迹由四个三趾脚印组成，两个左两个，右两个，可以追溯到 6650 万年前。一组科学家在北达科他州发现了第一组已知的成年霸王龙脚印。这条 23 英尺长的足迹由四个三趾脚印组成，两个左两个右，去年由科罗拉多州丹佛自然科学博物馆和英国利物浦约翰摩尔斯大学的研究人员首次在该州西南部的地狱溪地层恐龙化石区发现。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The discovery of these ancient T. rex footprints in North Dakota offers a profound glimpse into a world long past. It reminds us that creation itself, from the grandest dinosaur to the smallest creature, testifies to the wisdom and intricate design of its Creator. By studying these traces, we gain a deeper appreciation for the ancient world and the One who...
reflection.zh: 在北达科他州发现的这些古老的霸王龙足迹，让我们得以一窥早已逝去的世界。它提醒我们，整个受造界，从最庞大的恐龙到最小的生灵，都见证着其创造主的智慧和精妙的设计。通过研究这些痕迹，我们能更深刻地体会到古代世界以及那位安排这一切的“雅伟”的伟大。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Wasps are disappearing this summer, and scientists are worried
title.zh: 今年夏天黄蜂神秘消失，科学家们表示担忧

summary.en: Britain's common social wasps have become unusually scarce this summer, prompting concern among scientists. Researchers suspect that a combination of unusual temperature fluctuations, heatwaves, and a lack of food sources may be responsible for this decline. The wasps that are present also appear smaller than usual,...
summary.zh: 英国的常见社会黄蜂今年夏天数量异常稀少，引起了科学家的担忧。研究人员怀疑，反常的温度波动、热浪以及食物短缺的结合可能是导致这一衰退的原因。现存的黄蜂也比往常小，科学家认为这可能预示着极端环境条件对昆虫种群的影响。

body.en:
Summer can be lovely – until a wasp turns up. Whether they present as an irritating picnic visitor or an uninvited loft guest, common social wasps are as much a part of our summer as festivals, sun cream and the growing despair of how to entertain children who’ve forgotten how to be bored.

But summer 2026 is breaking the norm, and there don’t seem to be many wasps about. As a wasp biologist, I’ve noticed it acutely, because my students need wasps for their experiments, and we simply can’t find them.

A second sign that something is wrong is the absence of wasp stories in the media. Wasps tend to be more active in warmer weather. Their colonies grow faster and bigger, and they end up making news headlines by bothering humans. This time last year – also a warm spring and hot summer – the media airwaves were filled with “plagues of wasps” stories. Now, even professional pest-controllers tell me it’s a quiet year with very few requests to remove wasp nests.

Admittedly, these are anecdotes not data: the Big Wasp Survey – the only national wasp monitoring survey – is yet to start sampling this summer. But the signs are not good.

If data back this up, their absence worries me greatly because – love them or hate them – wasps are important in ecosystems as pest-controllers, pollinators and decomposers.

Spring started well for wasps. In the warm, dry spring a glut of glorious foundresses – new queens – emerged from hibernation to start their nests alone, carrying out all the nest building, egg laying, foraging and brood rearing. This nest-founding period is a risky time. If a new queen survives until her first brood emerges as adult workers, though, then the odds are in her favour as she no longer needs to undertake risky foraging.

But spring 2026 was strange: the warm, dry start should have been good. Warm, dry spring weather improves a nest’s chance of survival as it ensures a good nectar supply for the queen to develop her ovaries and good prey populations for her to feed the brood. But we experienced unprecedented heat for the time of year, punctuated by cold, damp days and followed by unexpectedly chilly nights.

Such weather extremes may have caused queens to abandon their nests or die, reducing the initial spring queen bounty to a more modest population.

And then came the heatwave. And another. And another. Some insects may benefit from this. Wildlife charity Butterfly Conservation is hoping 2026 could be a “ bumper summer of butterflies” because warm, dry days mean uninterrupted foraging, mating and egg-laying.

But all insects have a thermal tolerance called critical thermal maximum (CTmax). If their CTmax is exceeded, insects...
body.zh: 夏天可能很可爱——直到黄蜂出现。无论它们是令人恼火的野餐访客还是不请自来的阁楼客人，常见的社交黄蜂就像节日、防晒霜以及对如何娱乐那些忘记了如何无聊的孩子的日益绝望一样，都是我们夏天的一部分。 但 2026 年夏天打破了常态，周围似乎没有太多黄蜂。作为一名黄蜂生物学家，我敏锐地注意到了这一点，因为我的学生需要黄蜂进行实验，而我们根本找不到它们。 出现问题的第二个迹象是媒体上没有黄蜂故事。黄蜂在温暖的天气里往往更活跃。它们的群体生长得更快、更大，最终因为骚扰人类而成为新闻头条。去年这个时候，同样是温暖的春天和炎热的夏天，媒体广播中充斥着“黄蜂瘟疫”的故事。现在，即使是专业的害虫防治人员也告诉我，今年是安静的一年，很少有人要求清除黄蜂巢。 诚然，这些都是轶事而不是数据：大黄蜂调查——唯一的全国黄蜂监测调查——今年夏天尚未开始采样。但迹象并不好。 如果数据支持这一点，那么它们的消失让我非常担心，因为——无论爱它们还是恨它们——黄蜂在生态系统中作为害虫控制者、传粉者和分解者都很重要。 对于黄蜂来说，春天开始得很好。在温暖干燥的春天，大量光彩夺目的雌蜂——新蜂王——从冬眠中苏醒，独自筑巢，完成所有筑巢、产卵、觅食和育雏的工作。这个筑巢时期是一个危险的时期。不过，如果新蜂王能够存活到她的第一窝幼崽成为成年工蜂，那么机会对她有利，因为她不再需要进行危险的觅食。 但 2026 年的春天很奇怪：温暖、干燥的开局本应该是好的。温暖、干燥的春季天气提高了巢穴的生存机会，因为它确保了蜂王发育卵巢的良好花蜜供应和良好的猎物种群，以供其喂养巢穴。但我们经历了一年中前所未有的炎热天气，中间是寒冷潮湿的白天，随后是意想不到的寒冷夜晚。 这种极端天气可能导致蜂王放弃巢穴或死亡，从而将最初的春季蜂王赏金减少到较为有限的数量。 然后热浪来了。还有另一个。还有另一个。有些昆虫可能会从中受益。野生动物慈善机构蝴蝶保护组织希望 2026 年能够成为“蝴蝶的丰收之夏”，因为温暖干燥的日子意味着不间断的觅食、交配和产卵。 但所有昆虫都有一个耐热性，称为临界热最大值 (CTmax)。如果超过其 CTmax，昆虫...

reflection.en: The natural world, including the humble wasp, experiences distress and disruption due to environmental changes. As Romans 8:22 speaks of creation groaning, this scarcity reminds us that all of life is interconnected and affected by the world's condition. May we be mindful of our role in stewarding the earth and its creatures, seeking wisdom to address the...
reflection.zh: 自然界，包括不起眼的黄蜂，因环境变化而经历痛苦和动荡。正如罗马书8:22所说，万物都在呻吟，这种稀缺性提醒我们，所有生命都是相互联系的，并受到世界状况的影响。愿我们铭记自己在管理地球及其生物中的角色，寻求智慧来应对影响所有生物的环境挑战。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Sheen says he was snubbed by FM over pollution claims
title.zh: 希恩称因污染问题被财政大臣冷落

summary.en: The actor urged MPs to back a national testing programme to make sure historic toxic dump sites were safe.
summary.zh: 这位演员敦促议员们支持一项全国性的检测计划，以确保历史悠久的有毒垃圾填埋场是安全的。

reflection.en: Michael Sheen is using his platform to advocate for public safety, urging MPs to support a national testing program for toxic dump sites. His actions highlight the importance of speaking up for those who might be unknowingly exposed to environmental hazards, echoing the call to defend the vulnerable.
reflection.zh: 迈克尔·希恩正在利用他的平台倡导公众安全，敦促议员们支持一项针对有毒垃圾填埋场的全国性检测计划。他的行动突显了为那些可能在不知情的情况下暴露于环境危害中的人发声的重要性，呼应了为弱势群体辩护的呼吁。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: El Niño likely to cause wetter and warmer-than-normal autumn
title.zh: 厄尔尼诺可能导致比往常更湿润和温暖的秋季

summary.en: The UK is set for a warmer and wetter-than-normal autumn, according to the latest forecasts from the Met Office, driven by a strengthening El Niño phenomenon. This could help areas suffering from drought but also increase the risk of flooding.
summary.zh: 根据英国气象局的最新预测，受不断增强的厄尔尼诺现象影响，英国今年秋季将比往常更温暖湿润。这可能有助于缓解干旱地区的状况，但也可能增加洪水风险。

body.en:
The UK is set for wetter and warmer-than-normal weather this autumn, driven by a strengthening El Niño, according to the latest forecasts from the Met Office.

The climate phenomenon - forecast to be the strongest in living memory - will influence a change to stormier conditions later this season.

Potential wetter weather will put areas of the UK gripped by drought on the road to recovery, but it could also bring an increased chance of flooding as a result.

An already warming climate, paired with unusually high sea temperatures around the UK, will also contribute to above-average temperatures.

A stormy season is forecast for the UK with the chances of wet and windy weather higher than normal, particularly from November.

"The latest seasonal forecasts suggest an increased likelihood of wetter than average conditions as we move through autumn, which would be consistent with the historical influence of El Niño events," Met Office Chief Meteorologist Ian Lisk said.

El Niño - or the warming of the tropical Pacific Ocean - is continuing to strengthen and is expected peak in November or December as a historic event.

"While this event may become one of the strongest El Niño events on record, that does not automatically mean more severe impacts for the UK," he added.

A wetter outlook for late autumn and into winter will bring some relief to parched regions for the UK.

While the weather has recently turned more unsettled, there has so far been no change to the drought status, according to the Environment Agency (EA) National Drought Group, which met on Thursday.

Helen Wakeham, Director of Water at the EA said "drought recovery is a very long process" and only over once reservoirs, rivers and groundwater supplies are back to normal.

While the rainfall will be welcome, it is possible the UK could experience another round of "weather whiplash" where the pattern moves from one extreme to another.

A similar scenario played out in 2025 when the UK experienced a summer of record-breaking heat followed by storms and floods in the autumn.

It comes after summer 2026 was provisionally declared the hottest on record , following five widespread heatwaves and 40 days of temperatures above 30C (86F).

While a warmer-than-normal autumn is is consistent with global warming trends, the higher-than-normal sea surface temperatures around the UK will also have an influence.

The series of extreme heatwaves since late spring resulted in marine heatwaves , where sea surface temperatures have risen up to 5C above normal.

Warmer seas around the UK tend to keep land temperatures higher than they would otherwise normally be.

While it is unlikely the UK will see any snowfall this autumn, it is still too early to say if the winter will be especially cold or snowy.

El Niño...
body.zh: 根据英国气象局的最新预测，受厄尔尼诺现象增强的影响，今年秋天英国的天气将比正常情况更加潮湿和温暖。 这种气候现象——预计将是人们记忆中最强烈的——将影响本季晚些时候暴风雨天气的变化。 潜在的潮湿天气将使英国遭受干旱的地区走上复苏之路，但也可能导致洪水发生的可能性增加。 已经变暖的气候，加上英国各地异常高的海水温度，也将导致气温高于平均水平。 预计英国将迎来暴风雨季节，出现潮湿和多风天气的可能性高于正常水平，特别是从 11 月开始。 英国气象局首席气象学家伊恩·利斯克（Ian Lisk）表示：“最新的季节性预测表明，随着秋季的到来，降雨量高于平均水平的可能性会增加，这与厄尔尼诺事件的历史影响是一致的。” 厄尔尼诺现象（即热带太平洋变暖）正在继续加强，预计将在 11 月或 12 月达到峰值，成为历史性事件。 “虽然这一事件可能成为有记录以来最强烈的厄尔尼诺事件之一，但这并不自动意味着对英国的影响更严重，”他补充道。 深秋和冬季的湿润前景将为英国干旱地区带来一些缓解。 周四召开会议的环境署（EA）国家干旱小组表示，虽然最近天气变得更加不稳定，但干旱状况迄今为止没有任何变化。 EA 水务主管海伦·韦克汉姆 (Helen Wakeham) 表示，“干旱恢复是一个非常漫长的过程”，只有水库、河流和地下水供应恢复正常后才能恢复正常。 虽然降雨是受欢迎的，但英国可能会经历另一轮“天气鞭打”，模式从一个极端转向另一个极端。 2025 年也出现了类似的情况，当时英国经历了创纪录的夏季高温，随后在秋季发生了暴风雨和洪水。 在此之前，继五次大范围热浪和连续 40 天气温高于 30 摄氏度（86 华氏度）之后，2026 年夏季被临时宣布为有记录以来最热的夏季。 虽然秋季比正常温暖与全球变暖趋势一致，但英国周围高于正常的海面温度也会产生影响。 春末以来的一系列极端热浪导致海洋热浪，海面温度比正常水平高出5摄氏度。 英国周围温暖的海洋往往会使陆地温度高于正常水平。 虽然英国今年秋天不太可能下雪，但现在判断冬天是否会特别寒冷或下雪还为时过早。 厄尔尼诺现象...

reflection.en: The Met Office forecasts a warmer and wetter autumn for the UK, influenced by El Niño. While this may offer relief to drought-stricken areas, it also brings the potential for increased flooding. In times of environmental uncertainty and potential upheaval, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that God is our refuge and strength, a present help in times of trouble.
reflection.zh: 英国气象局预测，受厄尔尼诺现象影响，英国今年秋季将比往常更温暖湿润。虽然这可能为干旱地区带来缓解，但也带来了洪水加剧的潜在风险。在环境不确定和潜在动荡的时期，《诗篇》46:1提醒我们，神是我们的避难所和力量，是患难中随时的帮助。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Physicists just found a tiny glitch in time itself
title.zh: 物理学家刚刚发现了时间本身的一个微小瑕疵

summary.en: Unconventional quantum theories may imply that time itself has a tiny fundamental uncertainty, placing an ultimate limit on how precisely any clock could measure it. The effect is far beyond current detection, but it could reveal a hidden connection between quantum mechanics and the fundamental laws of the universe.
summary.zh: 非传统的量子理论可能意味着时间本身存在微小的基本不确定性，从而对任何时钟能够精确测量它的程度设定了最终限制。这种效应远远超出了当前的探测能力，但它可能揭示量子力学与宇宙基本定律之间隐藏的联系。

body.en:
Quantum mechanics has always challenged our everyday understanding of reality. In the quantum world, particles can exist in a superposition of states, meaning they can occupy multiple possible positions or configurations at the same time. Physicists describe these possibilities mathematically using a wavefunction.

That picture is very different from ordinary life, where an object appears to be in one place and one state at a time. To bridge that gap, standard quantum mechanics says that when a quantum system is measured or observed, its wavefunction collapses into a single definite outcome.

Now, with support from the Foundational Questions Institute, FQxI, an international team of physicists has explored a more radical possibility. Their work suggests that certain alternatives to standard quantum mechanics, known as quantum collapse models, could have surprising consequences for the nature of time itself and for the ultimate precision of clocks.

The findings, published in Physical Review Research , also point to a possible new way to test these unconventional theories against standard quantum mechanics.

"What we did was to take seriously the idea that collapse models may be linked to gravity," says Nicola Bortolotti, a PhD student at the Enrico Fermi Museum and Research Centre (CREF) in Rome, Italy, who led the study. "And then we asked a very concrete question: What does this imply for time itself?"

Beginning in the 1980s, physicists developed models in which wavefunction collapse does not require a measuring device or an observer. Instead, collapse can happen spontaneously.

That makes these ideas different from many interpretations of quantum mechanics. Interpretations mainly offer different conceptual explanations for what quantum theory means, while typically producing the same experimental predictions as standard quantum mechanics. Quantum collapse models go further because they predict physical effects that could, at least in principle, be measured.

Bortolotti and his colleagues examined two different collapse models. The team included Catalina Curceanu, a member of FQxI and research director at the Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati of the National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN-LNF) in Frascati, Italy, Kristian Piscicchia, at CREF and INFN-LNF, Lajos Diósi, of the Wigner Research Center for Physics and Eötvös Loránd University, in Budapest, Hungary, and Simone Manti of INFN-LNF.

One of the models was the Diósi-Penrose model (named after FQxI members Lajos Diósi and Sir Roger Penrose). It has long proposed that gravity may play a role in forcing quantum systems to collapse into definite states.

The researchers also studied a second approach called Continuous Spontaneous Localization. For the...
body.zh: 量子力学一直在挑战我们对现实的日常理解。在量子世界中，粒子可以以状态叠加的形式存在，这意味着它们可以同时占据多个可能的位置或配置。物理学家使用波函数在数学上描述了这些可能性。 这张照片与日常生活非常不同，在日常生活中，一个物体似乎一次处于一个地方、一种状态。为了弥合这一差距，标准量子力学表示，当测量或观察量子系统时，其波函数会塌陷为单个确定的结果。 现在，在基础问题研究所 FQxI 的支持下，一个国际物理学家团队探索了一种更激进的可能性。他们的工作表明，标准量子力学的某些替代方案（称为量子塌缩模型）可能会对时间本身的性质和时钟的最终精度产生令人惊讶的影响。 发表在《物理评论研究》上的研究结果还指出了一种可能的新方法，可以根据标准量子力学来测试这些非常规理论。 “我们所做的是认真对待塌陷模型可能与重力有关的想法，”领导这项研究的意大利罗马恩里科费米博物馆和研究中心（CREF）的博士生 Nicola Bortolotti 说。 “然后我们问了一个非常具体的问题：这对时间本身意味着什么？” 从 20 世纪 80 年代开始，物理学家开发了波函数塌缩不需要测量设备或观察者的模型。相反，崩溃可能会自发发生。 这使得这些想法不同于量子力学的许多解释。解释主要为量子理论的含义提供不同的概念解释，同时通常产生与标准量子力学相同的实验预测。量子塌缩模型走得更远，因为它们预测了至少在原则上可以测量的物理效应。 博尔托洛蒂和他的同事研究了两种不同的塌陷模型。该团队包括 FQxI 成员、意大利弗拉斯卡蒂国家核物理研究所 (INFN-LNF) 弗拉斯卡蒂国家实验室研究主任 Catalina Curceanu、CREF 和 INFN-LNF 的 Kristian Piscicchia、匈牙利布达佩斯维格纳物理研究中心和罗兰大学的 Lajos Diósi 以及 Simone Manti INFN-LNF。 其中一个模型是 Diósi-Penrose 模型（以 FQxI 成员 Lajos Diósi 和 Roger Penrose 爵士的名字命名）。长期以来，人们一直认为引力可能在迫使量子系统塌缩成确定状态方面发挥作用。 研究人员还研究了第二种方法，称为连续自发定位。对于...

reflection.en: The universe operates on principles that often elude our everyday grasp, as seen in the subtle 'glitch' physicists are exploring in the fabric of time. This pursuit of understanding the fundamental order, even in its smallest imperfections, echoes the profound truth that all things in creation are held together by a divine hand. As we ponder these deep...
reflection.zh: 宇宙的运行遵循着常常超出我们日常理解的规律，正如物理学家们正在探索的时间结构中那个微妙的“瑕疵”。这种对基本秩序的理解追求，即使是在其最小的不完美之处，也呼应了一个深刻的真理：创造中的万物都由一只神圣的手维系在一起。 当我们思考这些深刻的奥秘时，我们被提醒存在着精妙的设计，这是支撑现实的智慧和力量的证明。

verse.textEn: He is before all things, and in him all things hold together.
verse.textZh: 他在万有之先；万有也靠他而立。

title.en: Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park
title.zh: 威尔士最大国家公园一区域物种面临“消失风险”

summary.en: The National Trust has warned that several endangered species are on the verge of extinction in the Nant Ffrancon valley within Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park. A new £1 million conservation scheme aims to restore over 4,000 acres of habitat in the park.
summary.zh: 英国国家信托基金会警告称，在埃里里（斯诺登尼亚）国家公园内的南特弗兰孔山谷，一些濒危物种正濒临灭绝。一项新的耗资100万英镑的保护计划旨在恢复公园内超过4000英亩的栖息地。

body.en:
Some of Wales' most endangered species are "at risk of vanishing" from an area of the country's largest national park, experts have warned.

The National Trust said Nant Ffrancon, a valley in Eryri National Park, was facing "serious ecological decline" with some species in danger of disappearing altogether, including the mountain blackbird and the mountain finch.

Now, a new £1m scheme is aiming to restore and conserve more than 4,000 acres of habitats at Eryri, also known as Snowdonia .

"We're in a very serious situation - we're in a nature emergency. There are so many species in this valley which are on the brink of extinction," said Simon Rogers from the National Trust.

From the high peaks of Cwm Idwal to the deep valleys of Dyffryn Ogwen, Nant Ffrancon is one of the most special and unique landscapes in Wales.

But experts say its habitat has deteriorated and some of Wales' most threatened species, including the ring ouzel bird, are in danger of disappearing altogether.

Now, a project led by the National Trust will work together with local communities, tenant farmers and volunteers to restore and protect 4,040 acres of habitats.

Rogers said there was a "unique variety of habitats" in the area and warned many species "really are on the brink".

"One of the ones we've chosen to look at particularly in this project is the ring ouzel - a bird that's red-listed," he explained.

"It's been in decline massively in the area and across the whole country, and this is one of the last strongholds for it.

"So we'll be looking at that little bird, understanding how they use the landscape here and doing our best to manage the land to ensure their survival for the future.

"There are a lot arctic alpine flowers that grow in Cwm Idwal as well, one of them being the Tufted Saxifrage, where there were only seven individuals at the start of the year - all of them growing here in Cwm Idwal.

"But with the drought we've had this year, only three have made it through the summer. That's three through the whole of Wales, so they're at a very real risk of extinction if we don't do something about it."

Another project which will benefit is Tlysau Mynydd Eryri (Mountain Jewels of Eryri), part of a conservation partnership led by Plantlife Cymru to protect the future of some of the rarest alpine plants in Wales.

Ecological surveys and regular monitoring will map the impact of the restoration work, using species such as the woodcock and otter, and plants including aspen and juniper to give an idea of the health of the valley.

The work will also build on innovative use of GPS livestock collars to manage grazing more precisely.

body.zh: 专家警告说，威尔士最大的国家公园的一些最濒危物种正面临“消失的危险”。 国家信托基金会表示，埃里里国家公园内的一个山谷南特弗兰孔正面临“严重的生态衰退”，一些物种面临完全消失的危险，包括山黑鸟和山雀。 现在，一项耗资 100 万英镑的新计划旨在恢复和保护 Eryri（也称为 Snowdonia）超过 4,000 英亩的栖息地。 “我们的处境非常严峻——我们正处于自然紧急状态。这个山谷中有很多物种正处于灭绝的边缘，”国家信托基金的西蒙·罗杰斯说。 从 Cwm Idwal 的高峰到 Dyffryn Ogwen 的深谷，南特弗兰孔 (Nant Ffrancon) 是威尔士最特殊、最独特的景观之一。 但专家表示，其栖息地已经恶化，威尔士一些最受威胁的物种，包括环乌泽尔鸟，正面临完全消失的危险。 现在，由国家信托基金会领导的一个项目将与当地社区、佃农和志愿者合作，恢复和保护 4,040 英亩的栖息地。 罗杰斯说，该地区有“独特的多种栖息地”，并警告许多物种“确实处于濒临灭绝的边缘”。 “我们在这个项目中选择特别关注的鸟类之一是环乌泽尔 - 一种被列入红色名单的鸟类，”他解释道。 “它在该地区和全国范围内都在大幅下降，而这是它最后的据点之一。 “因此，我们将关注这只小鸟，了解它们如何利用这里的景观，并尽最大努力管理这片土地，以确保它们未来的生存。 “Cwm Idwal 也生长着许多北极高山花卉，其中之一是簇绒虎耳草，今年年初那里只有七株 - 它们都生长在 Cwm Idwal。 “但是由于今年的干旱，只有三个人度过了夏天。整个威尔士有三只，所以如果我们不采取措施，它们就面临着灭绝的危险。” 另一个受益的项目是 Tlysau Mynydd Eryri（Eryri 山宝石），该项目是 Plantlife Cymru 领导的保护伙伴关系的一部分，旨在保护威尔士一些最稀有的高山植物的未来。 生态调查和定期监测将利用山鹬和水獭等物种以及白杨和杜松等植物来绘制恢复工作的影响，以了解山谷的健康状况。 这项工作还将以 GPS 牲畜项圈的创新应用为基础，以更精确地管理放牧。 Cwm Idwal 合作伙伴官员 Rhys Wheldon-Roberts 表示，监测“非常重要，因为它使我们能够在正确的区域放牧......

reflection.en: The warning from the National Trust about species facing extinction in Eryri National Park underscores a profound ecological crisis. It calls us to remember that the Earth and all its creatures are ultimately the possession of Yahweh, and we are called to be stewards of His creation. As we witness the decline of species like the mountain blackbird and...
reflection.zh: 英国国家信托基金会关于埃里里国家公园物种濒临灭绝的警告，凸显了严峻的生态危机。这提醒我们，大地及其万物最终属于雅伟，而我们被呼召成为祂所造之物的管家。 当我们目睹山地乌鸫和山雀等物种的衰落时，我们被提醒要承担起照管托付给我们的大自然的责任，寻求其复兴与繁荣。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Weatherwatch: soil moisture deficit – how dry are the UK’s thirsty soils?
title.zh: 天气观察：土壤水分赤字——英国干渴的土壤有多干？

summary.en: Soil moisture deficit (SMD) is the amount of moisture the soil needs to reach its full capacity. Very dry conditions are currently affecting most of England and Wales. Meteorologists use SMD to define drought, measuring it in millimeters of rain needed to replenish the soil. Typically, southern England's SMD is near...
summary.zh: 土壤水分赤字（SMD）是指土壤需要补充多少水分才能达到其容量。目前，英格兰和威尔士大部分地区正经历严重干旱。气象学家使用SMD来定义干旱，以需要多少毫米的降雨来补充土壤至其容量来衡量。通常，英格兰南部冬季的SMD接近零，但在干旱年份的夏季可能达到100-150毫米或更高，当土壤中没有植物可利用的水分时，就会出现极端干旱...

body.en: SMD is the moisture the soil must make up until it is at capacity, with very dry conditions over most of England and Wales When the ground is thoroughly wet, after excess rainwater has run off it is said to be at field capacity. Meteorologists describe drought in terms of soil moisture deficit (SMD) from field capacity. The SMD is a measure of how thirsty the soil is, expressed as how many millimetres of rain it would take to top it up to field capacity. In southern England, the SMD tends to hover around zero in winter when fields are wet. In summer it may be about 100mm, going up to 150mm or more in a dry year. The extreme of dryness, when soil has no water accessible to plants, is known as the permanent wilting point or PWP. Continue reading...
body.zh: SMD 是土壤在达到容量之前必须补充的水分，英格兰和威尔士大部分地区的条件非常干燥。当地面完全湿润时，多余的雨水流失后，就可以说达到了田间容量。气象学家根据田间容量的土壤水分亏缺（SMD）来描述干旱。 SMD 是土壤干渴程度的衡量标准，表示为需要多少毫米的降雨才能达到田间容量。在英格兰南部，冬季田地潮湿时，SMD 往往徘徊在零附近。夏季，水深可能约为 100 毫米，干旱年份可达 150 毫米或更高。当土壤没有水可供植物吸收时，极端干燥被称为永久萎蔫点或 PWP。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The scientific measurement of soil moisture deficit reveals the land's deep thirst. This detailed observation of creation's condition reminds us of the intricate systems Yahweh has put in place. The wisdom in understanding these natural processes points to the Creator's profound design.
reflection.zh: 对土壤水分赤字的科学测量揭示了土地的深切干渴。对受造界状况的这种细致观察，提醒我们雅伟所设立的错综复杂的系统。理解这些自然过程的智慧，指向了创造主的深邃设计。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Scientists discover the human heart can regrow muscle after a heart attack
title.zh: 科学家发现人类心脏在心脏病发作后可以再生肌肉

summary.en: For the first time, researchers have demonstrated that human heart muscle cells can regenerate after a heart attack, challenging the long-standing belief that damaged heart tissue is incapable of regrowth. This finding opens avenues for developing new treatments for cardiovascular disease.
summary.zh: 研究人员首次证明，人类心肌细胞在心脏病发作后能够再生，这挑战了长期以来认为受损心脏组织无法再生的观点。这一发现为开发心血管疾病的新疗法开辟了道路。

body.en:
Researchers from the University of Sydney, the Baird Institute and Royal Prince Alfred Hospital in Sydney have found that the human heart can produce new muscle cells after a heart attack. The discovery challenges the long-held assumption that heart muscle lost during an attack cannot regenerate and could eventually help scientists develop new treatments for cardiovascular disease.

The findings were published in Circulation Research . First author Dr. Robert Hume, from the Faculty of Medicine and Health and Charles Perkins Centre, and Lead of Translational Research at the Baird Institute for Applied Heart and Lung Research, explained why the result could be important.

"Until now we've thought that, because heart cells die after a heart attack, those areas of the heart were irreparably damaged, leaving the heart less able to pump blood to the body's organs.

"Our research shows that while the heart is left scarred after a heart attack, it produces new muscle cells, which opens up new possibilities.

"Although this new discovery of regrowing muscle cells is exciting, it isn't enough to prevent the devastating effects of a heart attack. Therefore, in time, we hope to develop therapies that can amplify the heart's natural ability to produce new cells and regenerate the heart after an attack."

Scientists had previously seen increased mitosis (a process in which cells divide and reproduce) in the heart muscles of mice following a heart attack. The new research is the first to demonstrate the same phenomenon in humans.

The heart's natural regenerative response is not currently strong enough to replace all of the muscle destroyed during a heart attack. However, understanding how this process works could help researchers find ways to increase it.

Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide. In Australia, it accounts for nearly a quarter (24 percent) of all deaths.

A heart attack can destroy as many as one third of the cells in the human heart. Although advances in treatment have dramatically improved survival over the past decade, surviving the initial attack does not always prevent serious long-term consequences.

Many patients eventually develop heart failure, a condition in which the heart can no longer pump blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs. A heart transplant is currently the only cure for heart failure.

That option is available to only a small fraction of patients. Australia has approximately 144,000 people living with heart failure, while only about 115 heart transplants are performed each year. That leaves a major gap between the number of patients who could benefit from a new heart and the number of donor organs available.

The research also relied on a world-first approach involving heart tissue...
body.zh: 来自悉尼大学、贝尔德研究所和悉尼皇家阿尔弗雷德王子医院的研究人员发现，人类心脏在心脏病发作后可以产生新的肌肉细胞。这一发现挑战了人们长期以来的假设，即在发作期间失去的心肌无法再生，并最终可能帮助科学家开发出治疗心血管疾病的新疗法。 研究结果发表在《循环研究》上。第一作者、来自医学与健康学院和查尔斯·珀金斯中心、贝尔德应用心肺研究所转化研究负责人的罗伯特·休姆博士解释了为什么这一结果可能很重要。 “到目前为止，我们一直认为，由于心脏细胞在心脏病发作后死亡，心脏的这些区域受到了不可挽回的损害，导致心脏无法将血液泵送到身体的器官。 “我们的研究表明，虽然心脏病发作后心脏会留下疤痕，但它会产生新的肌肉细胞，这开辟了新的可能性。 “虽然肌肉细胞再生的这一新发现令人兴奋，但这还不足以防止心脏病发作的破坏性影响。因此，我们希望及时开发出能够增强心脏产生新细胞的自然能力并在心脏病发作后再生心脏的疗法。” 科学家此前曾发现心脏病发作后小鼠的心肌有丝分裂（细胞分裂和繁殖的过程）增加。这项新研究首次在人类身上证明了同样的现象。 目前，心脏的自然再生反应还不足以替代心脏病发作期间受损的所有肌肉。然而，了解这个过程是如何运作的可以帮助研究人员找到增加它的方法。 心血管疾病仍然是全世界死亡的主要原因。在澳大利亚，它占所有死亡人数的近四分之一（24%）。 心脏病发作可以破坏人类心脏中多达三分之一的细胞。尽管过去十年来治疗方法的进步极大地提高了生存率，但在初次发作中幸存下来并不总能避免严重的长期后果。 许多患者最终会出现心力衰竭，即心脏无法有效地泵血来满足身体的需要。心脏移植是目前治疗心力衰竭的唯一方法。 这种选择只适用于一小部分患者。澳大利亚约有 144,000 名心力衰竭患者，而每年仅进行约 115 例心脏移植手术。这使得可以从新心脏中受益的患者数量与可用的捐赠器官数量之间存在巨大差距。 该研究还依赖于世界首创的涉及心脏组织的方法......

reflection.en: The discovery that human heart muscle can regenerate after damage is a testament to the intricate design of the human body. It reminds us that even in areas once thought to be beyond repair, Yahweh's creation holds surprising capacities for renewal. This scientific insight invites us to marvel at the complexity of life and to seek wisdom in understanding...
reflection.zh: 人类心肌在受损后能够再生的发现，证明了人体设计的精妙。它提醒我们，即使在曾经被认为无法修复的领域，雅伟的创造也蕴藏着令人惊讶的更新能力。这一科学见解邀请我们惊叹于生命的复杂性，并在理解祂的杰作中寻求智慧。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Briefing Chat: The Bunsen burner myth that turns out to be just hot air
title.zh: 简报聊天：事实证明，本生灯的消毒神话不过是些空谈

summary.en: Nature staff discuss an AI tool that can assess the impact of 9 billion mutations—plus, how the Bunsen burner’s reputation for sterilization might be based on tradition alone.
summary.zh: 《自然》杂志的员工讨论了一种可以评估90亿个突变影响的人工智能工具，此外，还探讨了本生灯的消毒声誉可能仅仅基于传统。

reflection.en: The relentless march of scientific discovery, exemplified by an AI tool analyzing billions of mutations, reflects a world where knowledge is rapidly expanding. As we gain unprecedented insights into the natural world, may we also seek the wisdom to use this knowledge for good, remembering that true understanding is rooted in reverence for the Creator.
reflection.zh: 科学发现的不断进步，例如分析数十亿个突变的人工智能工具，反映了一个知识迅速增长的世界。当我们对自然界获得前所未有的见解时，愿我们也寻求智慧，将这些知识用于善事，并牢记真正的理解根植于对造物主的敬畏之中。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。
